name: Varbase Components
description: Components handler for the Varbase distribution: installs and wires up the UI Patterns + UI Icons SDC theming stack via a recipe, exposes an active_theme Twig variable, and auto-migrates theme references in config when the default theme changes.
project_description:
Varbase Components is the components-handler module of the Varbase distribution. It does not ship any Single Directory Components, Twig templates, libraries, or config of its own; instead it is the glue that stands up and maintains a component-based theming stack for Varbase and Vartheme BS5 (Bootstrap 5, SASS, SDC, UI Patterns).

On install it runs a bundled core recipe (recipes/default) that installs and imports the config of the UI Patterns family (ui_patterns, ui_patterns_layouts, ui_patterns_library, ui_patterns_views, ui_patterns_field_formatters, ui_patterns_field_group, ui_patterns_ds) and the UI Icons family (ui_icons, ui_icons_patterns, ui_icons_field, ui_icons_picker, ui_icons_library). Its composer requirements also pull in ds, field_group and storybook.

At runtime it does two small things. A #[Hook('preprocess')] implementation exposes the site's default theme machine name to every template as the active_theme variable, so Varbase/Vartheme component templates can reference it. An ActiveThemeChangeSubscriber listens on config SAVE and, when the default theme (system.theme:default) changes AND both the old and new themes declare auto_switch_components: true in their .info.yml, performs a bulk find-and-replace of the old theme machine name with the new one across all active configuration (notably core.entity_view_display.* entries and config dependencies.theme lists). This keeps component/UI Patterns configuration bound to a Vartheme subtheme working after the site is re-themed to a sibling subtheme.

The module pins core to ~11.4.0, so installing it ties the site's core updates to the Varbase release cycle. It is intended to travel with the Varbase distribution, though it can technically be installed on any compatible Drupal site. Sponsored and developed by Vardot.
